clue.text: Lift a seabird, opening bill

indicators.note: the seabird phrase forces the bill open and sits in the gap it makes

parts.note: a bill is a printed notice or poster pasted on a wall
a tern is a gull-like seabird

explanation.surface: Someone hoists a seabird while opening a bill, a puzzling domestic scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lift' reads as a verb, but it is a noun: a kind of lift. 'opening' says the bill is split to take the seabird.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a type of elevator with open cars on a continuous loop, and lift is the British word for an elevator.

clue.text: Annoyed to get this tiny bit of fruit

definitions.meaning: in a British idiom, to get or have this seed means to be irritated or fed up
a small seed found in an apple or orange

explanation.surface: Someone is cross at finding a tiny scrap of fruit in their food.
explanation.definitionFit: A small seed of an apple or citrus fruit, which the British idiom also uses for a fit of annoyance.

clue.text: Tie sported by elegant Russian

indicators.note: sported by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A stylish Russian man is wearing a necktie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tie' looks like the necktie the Russian is wearing, but it is the verb: to tie up or bind.
explanation.definitionFit: To bind something up tightly, as a cook does to a chicken's legs, is a synonym of tie.

clue.text: Soldier raising artillery weapon

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery
a Luger is a German pistol

explanation.surface: A soldier lifts up an artillery piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' turns RA + LUGER upside down in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional, full-time member of a standing army, as opposed to a reservist, is called this kind of soldier.

clue.text: Humorist's hand's gone fluttering

indicators.note: fluttering suggests the letters flapping about and settling in a new order

explanation.surface: A comic writer's hand trembles and is lost, like a nervous gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fluttering' shuffles HANDSGONE; the 's after Humorist is a link ('is').
explanation.definitionFit: The American writer famous for witty light verse, a classic example of a humorist.

clue.text: Home key too fine for filing down

indicators.note: filing down wears each word away at its end, so each loses its last letter

parts.note: too as written, and fine means nice

explanation.surface: A craftsman's guide: the house key is too delicate to be filed down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filing down' trims both TOO and NICE of their last letters, giving TO + NIC.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, the keynote or first degree of a scale is where the melody comes home.

clue.text: Us State treasury perhaps more full than any other

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state
a chest is a box where treasure is kept

explanation.surface: The coffers of an American state are perhaps the fullest of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks a chest as just one example of a treasury.
explanation.definitionFit: Rich can mean abundantly supplied or plentiful, so the superlative means fullest of all.

clue.text: Step back to see tunnel

indicators.note: back says the word for a step is turned around and read right to left

parts.note: a pas is a dance step

explanation.surface: An instruction to take a pace backwards to look at a tunnel.
explanation.definitionFit: A trench or tunnel dug to approach or undermine a fortification is a military term for one.

clue.text: Game is over — battle, as you see, just starting

indicators.note: over says the little word is flipped round, read in the other direction

parts.note: taken as written
Mons was a First World War battle in Belgium

indicators.note: just starting takes only the opening letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A war reporter's line: the game is up, the battle, as you can tell, only beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns IS into SI; 'just starting' gives A, Y and S from 'as you see'.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's party game in which players obey only orders prefaced by a leader's name.

clue.text: Gain position to snaffle last of the pastry

indicators.note: to snaffle is to grab and hold, so the pair of words takes a letter into their middle

parts.note: a profit is a gain
a role is a position or job

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone seeks advantage by grabbing the last remaining pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gain' and 'position' sit side by side, and 'to snaffle' has them grab E between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A small choux bun filled with cream and covered in chocolate sauce is a classic French pastry.

clue.text: Connected up, having projections inside fastener

indicators.note: inside says one piece sits within the fastener's letters

parts.note: a pin fastens things together
lugs are projecting handles or ears, so something lugged has projections

explanation.surface: A technical description of a clip with protruding tabs inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An appliance attached to the mains through its plug and socket is connected up and ready to work.

clue.text: Attended old picture

parts.note: came means attended, as in came to the party

explanation.surface: Someone went to see an old film or painting.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved relief portrait, often in profile on a brooch, is a small picture.

clue.text: With temperature failing, damage medically — one new hormone

indicators.note: failing says the temperature letter drops out of the word it was in

parts.note: in medicine an insult is an injury or harm to the body
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A medical warning: if the temperature drops, harm is done, and one hormone is new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'medically' points to the doctor's sense of insult; 'failing' removes T, leaving INSUL.
explanation.definitionFit: The pancreatic hormone that regulates blood sugar, used to treat diabetes.

clue.text: Bugging may give Etonian fits

indicators.note: may give suggests the letters can be reworked to produce something new

explanation.surface: Being pestered might drive a schoolboy from Eton into tantrums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bugging' looks like annoying the boy; it means being overrun with insects. 'may give' rearranges ETONIANFITS.
explanation.definitionFit: A house overrun by insects or other pests is bugged in the literal sense, plagued by bugs.

clue.text: City councillor's first one to admit hair colouring

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the pair opens to take in the dye
first takes just the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
henna is a reddish dye used on hair

explanation.surface: A city councillor is the first to confess to dyeing their hair.
explanation.walkthrough: C and I take HENNA between them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian city formerly called Madras, capital of Tamil Nadu.

clue.text: Two couples eating large meal

indicators.note: eating means the number swallows a letter into its middle

parts.note: two pairs make four

explanation.surface: Two pairs of diners tucking into a big dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meal' looks like dinner, but it is ground grain.
explanation.definitionFit: Meal is grain ground to powder, and the finely milled wheat used in baking is the same thing.

clue.text: Independently thereby deny scattering wild oats?

definitions.meaning: a protest that no wild oats were sown

explanation.surface: A young man protests his chastity, insisting he has sown no wild oats at all.
explanation.walkthrough: To sow wild oats is to have a fling in youth. Respaced, the letters read 'O, none sown'.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something by yourself, unaided and alone, is the meaning of the idiom.

clue.text: Making a turn right, into a little paddy

indicators.note: into says the letter for right is put inside the phrase that follows

parts.note: a bit is a little
in British usage a paddy is a fit of temper

explanation.surface: Someone turning right drives into a small rice field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' is the trader's profit, not a change of direction; 'paddy' is a British word for a temper, not a rice field.
explanation.definitionFit: Buying and selling an asset in different markets for profit; a turn is the trader's margin.

clue.text: A cry of appreciation, seafood being served up, here?

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the letters are presented reading upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: Where might one hear applause while being served seafood?
explanation.walkthrough: AN OLE + CRAB, read upwards. The question mark flags that 'here' is the place where olés and seafood are found.
explanation.definitionFit: The Catalan city famous for seafood, where a Spanish cry of approval is at home.

clue.text: Cover for chest most unusually gets longer

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of the word before it appear in an unusual order

parts.note: read as one who longs, a longer is one who aches for something

explanation.surface: A garment covering the chest grows much longer than expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'longer' looks like 'more long', but it is one who longs. 'unusually' rearranges MOST into STOM.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornamental panel worn over the chest and stomach under a laced bodice in older fashions.

clue.text: Such lies being challenged?

definitions.meaning: split as '...', as in the phrase ... of lies

explanation.surface: Falsehoods of this sort are being questioned.
explanation.walkthrough: A tissue of lies is a web of untruths, so the letters split as 'a tissue' describe such lies.
explanation.definitionFit: A point in dispute, the matter under debate, is the point being challenged.

clue.text: Keenness to get summer month over, having missed gold

indicators.note: having missed says the gold letters are lost from the month

parts.note: August is a summer month in the northern hemisphere
AU is the chemical symbol for gold
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Someone's enthusiasm for summer drops when they miss out on a gold medal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearty enjoyment and zest in doing something is the same as eagerness or keenness.

clue.text: One relatively old to be married in good golf club

indicators.note: in places the married letter inside the club's letters

parts.note: the R and A is the Royal and Ancient Golf Club of St Andrews

explanation.surface: An older person getting married at a fine golf club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relatively' means as a relative: an old family member, not someone fairly old.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandmother is an older family member, literally a relative who is old.

clue.text: A bank clerk, needing to change a pound for one, finds workroom

indicators.note: needing to change says one letter is swapped out for another

parts.note: a teller is a bank clerk
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A bank clerk swaps a pound coin for a one and then finds a workroom.
explanation.walkthrough: In A TELLER the second L becomes I.

clue.text: Book into base, finding not a living soul

indicators.note: into says the book letter goes inside the word for base

parts.note: a root is a base or foundation

explanation.surface: Someone takes a book into a base and finds the place deserted.

clue.text: Paper one's taken from heap, for instance

parts.note: a pile is a heap
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.walkthrough: 'for instance' is the familiar phrase, but only 'instance' defines; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A specimen or case that illustrates something is a synonym of instance.

clue.text: Virtually idle in secretary's place, literally

indicators.note: in puts the shortened word inside the secretary's letters

clue.text: Deals with clothes, say, several of which may be in the fire

definitions.text: several of which may be in the fire

clue.text: Medium large belt

a band is a belt or strip

clue.text: Nobody sounds religious

parts.note: none means not one person, nobody

explanation.walkthrough: 'religious' is a noun here: a member of a religious order.
